question: What do the joints cost, what is reuse worth, and what keeps two graphs apart?

versions.ffmpeg: ffmpeg version 2025-02-06-git-6da82b4485-full_build-www.gyan.dev Copyright (c) 2000-2025 the FFmpeg developers

notes: ISOLATED: resident frames, one thread, no store, no fill, no drawing. Right instrument for arithmetic against arithmetic and the wrong one for anything felt. Not to be quoted as a loop cost.
decoded 220 rows at 2144+982+1024x1024@1024x1024:gray in 1654 ms (7.52 ms/frame, sequential software decode) — the figure the crossover case is expressed against
joints: 0.2 us per edge, from a 4-edge chain over a 64x64 array, where the work is small enough for a joint to resolve
joints at the analysis form: fused 0.991 ms/position, staged 1.131 ms, difference +0.140 ms against a noise floor of 0.027 ms — resolvable

joints, read: 0.2 us an edge at 64x64 and 140 us at the analysis form — 560x for 256x the pixels, so an edge costs the intermediate it names and not the call that names it. At the analysis form a ten-edge graph spends about 1.40 ms on joints, which is 4% of a 30 fps period. Generality is affordable; it is not free, and it is priced in bytes touched.
reuse[diff]: reuse 2, recompute 1.120 ms/position, keep 0.317 ms, holding 121 intermediates (126.9 MB)
reuse[mhi]: reuse 4, recompute 4.246 ms/position, keep 2.953 ms, holding 150 intermediates (157.3 MB)

reuse, read: a declared reuse of 2 saved 0.803 ms/position and a declared reuse of 4 saved 1.293 ms — the saving grows with the declared reuse, so a scheduler can predict from a declaration what keeping an intermediate buys.

crossover: over 240 positions keeping saved 532 ms while the same 150 arrays' worth of room would have avoided 1128 ms of decode at this machine's 7.52 ms/frame — 0.47x, so spending the bytes on frames wins here.

crossover break-even: 3.55 ms per frame. A fetch dearer than that makes the room worth more as frames; a fetch cheaper than that makes the intermediate worth keeping. The verdict is not the result — the threshold is, because a session reads frames from a decode, a chunk and a proxy at costs that straddle it.

crossover, how far to trust it: the threshold is a ratio of two timings and moves by more between runs than either does within one, so it is an order-of-magnitude claim and not a figure to branch on. What it is being read for is which side of it the tiers sit, and successive runs in results/ are where a later one supersedes this.
key: two graphs differing only upstream filed under 2 key(s); values differ by 1.3602 at most
joints (what an edge costs): 3 checked, 0 disagreed
key (upstream reaches the name): 3 checked, 0 disagreed

params.note: the noise floor: the same work measured twice
